plan:
Mosaic only allows a sublane-strided load from a base memref whose last dim is exactly 128, so a single (1024, 256) f32 staging scratch cannot be used.
The f32 staging scratch is split into W//128 separate (cp*H, 128) f32 buffers (one per 128-lane column group); each chunk is cast bf16->f32 into them
and H pooling is 4 stride-4 sublane loads + max per buffer, so every strided load reads a 128-wide base memref (offsets 0..3, static).
W pooling: the 128-lane groups are concatenated (aligned) and one bf16 MXU matmul with an iota-built 0/1 matrix packs the 4 lane phases into 2 aligned
128-lane groups (phase pairs side by side, 64 lanes each); max over the groups, then max with a 64-lane roll (direction-agnostic half-rotation) finishes it.
1-D "parallel" grid over 4 MiB blocks of 32 planes of the free (N*C*H, W) view, output (N*C*Ho, Wo) bf16; x read from HBM once.

Grid (N, C/Cb), Cb=32: blocks (1,32,128,128) f32 = 2 MB for x, y and out (12 MB double-buffered, limit 40 MB).
a, b (C,) f32 placed whole in SMEM; fori over the Cb channels: o[0,ci] = a[c]*x[0,ci] + b[c]*y[0,ci] (scalar broadcast).
Nothing outside the kernel. Speed idea: exactly one read of x, y and one write, no relayout copies.
(Equal spatial shapes, as here; the bilinear-resize branch of the reference is not taken.)

Grid (B*D1*D2/16384,) sequential, blocks (16384, 128) bf16 = 4 MiB per input, double-buffered (16 MiB).
f32 error and max((q-1)e, qe), folded per 64-row chunk into an (8,128) f32 carry; f32 VMEM accumulator across steps.
Outside: bitcast reshape to (B*D1*D2, D3), final (1,1)->() reshape and astype only.
Speed idea: keeping the native lane dim avoids relayout copies; mean(sum over dim1) = total * D1 / numel, one HBM pass.

Grid (B, H/th) both parallel; x block (1, C, th, W) native layout, th multiple of 8 with C*th*W*4 ~ 4 MB (th=32 here).
f32 carry (th, W): fori_loop over channels accumulates x^2 (leading-dim indexing, elementwise adds), inv = rsqrt(sum/C + eps).
Second fori_loop writes o[c] = x[c] * inv. Nothing outside the kernel (no reshape).
Speed idea: no relayout copies, one HBM read + one write, register-resident reduction with no cross-lane/sublane work.

Kernel 1: grid (I/8, J/128); block (O, 8, 128) f32 of W, softmax over O per i via 128-lane strided loads; output
softmax(W) as (I, O, J) bf16 so each i is a contiguous (O, J) slab.
Kernel 2: grid (M/1024 rows, I/16 chunks); x tiles transposed once per row tile into VMEM (x1^T f32, x2^T bf16),
U[(i,j), m] = x1[m,i] * x2[m,j] built in bf16 for 8 i at a time and multiplied by the 8 slabs concatenated
along lanes (K = 2048) on the MXU into an (O, 1024) f32 accumulator; last chunk normalises by the sum over O,
transposes and stores (1024, O). Outside: leading-dim reshapes only.

Two pallas_calls, both grid (B, D) with x blocks (1, C, 1, H, W) = 1 MiB bf16 on the native 5D array (no relayout).
Stats (arbitrary): per step a (C, C*H) 0/1 selector @ x (C*H, W) on the MXU (exact f32) gives the H-sum; ones(8,W) @ t.T the per-d channel totals;
an f32 (C*H, W) accumulator over D gives the W-sums. At d = D-1 the w1 projections (bf16 hi/lo splits, ~f32 accurate) give Pw (Cr, W) and Q (D, Cr, H).
Apply (parallel): for each h, relu(Pw + Q[:, h]) in bf16 @ w2^T on the MXU, sigmoid via tanh, strided store into a (C*H, W) f32 gate; out = x * gate.
Outside only transposes/broadcast/reshape of the tiny weights and bias astype.

Grid (B, C/cb) with block (1, cb, H, W) = (1, 16, 256, 256) bf16 = 2 MiB on the native NCHW layout (no reshape of x).
lam reshaped to (C,) f32 and placed in SMEM; per channel t = lam*sigma^2/L as a scalar, out = x - clip(x, -t, t) in f32, cast to bf16 on store.
Nothing else outside the kernel. Speed idea: one read and one write of x with no relayout copies.

Grid (N, H/32), block (C, 32, W) of x plus 8-row halo blocks above/below; output block (C, 32, W). bf16 MXU, f32 accumulation.
In kernel: spectral-norm 1/sigma by exact f32 VPU reductions; input rows copied into 128-lane slabs, gathered per row into a bf16
(34*C, W) stacked-row scratch; per output row one (3Co, 3Ci) @ (3C, W) matmul, kw shifts by lane roll + edge mask, scale, bias,
LeakyReLU, residual; rows stored through 128-lane slabs (strided store) then copied to the output block.
Outside: only the weight transpose/reshape/astype and bias/u reshapes. Speed: x read once (+1/4 halo), output written once.

Grid (B, C/64): x block (1, 64, H, W) f32 = 4 MiB (double-buffered 8 MiB); w (C, N) and bias as constant full blocks (fetched once).
Per channel: f32 sum over (H, W) to a (1,1) value, times that channel's w row, accumulated in f32; output row (1,1,N) stays
resident over the channel axis, initialised with the bias.
Outside: only the (B,1,N)->(B,N) reshape of the 64 KiB result; x keeps its native layout (an H*W reshape would be a full copy).
Speed idea: one HBM read of x at full bandwidth; all math is tiny VPU work hidden under the DMA.

Layout: x is transposed once outside to NHCW (N, H, C, W) so an image row of all channels is a plain (C, W) block; the output is transposed back. No strided loads are needed.
Conv kernels, grid (N, H/32) (parallel, arbitrary): block (1, 32, C, W) f32 plus one-row halo blocks above/below; each window row becomes 3 lane-shifted copies split into bf16 hi/lo patches (34, 3C, W).
Per 4 output rows and kernel row kh: (Co, 3C) @ (3C, 4W) in bf16x3 (hi*hi + lo*hi + hi*lo) with f32 accumulation, matching the HIGHEST-precision reference.
InstanceNorm stats (sum, sum of squares, lane-partial (Co,128)) accumulate in a resident output across the row axis; conv2 applies relu(IN1) to its input on load.
Final kernel: relu(x + IN2(y2)) on NHCW blocks.

Grid (n/2,) "arbitrary": lp block (2, l, V) f32 native layout (4 MB); seq^T, prev^T (int32) and reward^T (l, n) full blocks (lane-dense, fetched once); (8,128) f32 scratch accumulator.
Per batch row b: column of seq/weight via masked lane-sum over the (l, n) arrays -> (l,1); weight = -reward*(prev>0).
Per 8 timesteps (static unroll, 16 groups): d = seq - lane_iota; acc8 = sum_k where(d == 128k, x[:, k*128:(k+1)*128], 0) (vreg adds only), then acc += acc8 * weight.
Last step: num = sum(acc), den = sum(prev>0) over (l, n), output num/den as (1,1) f32; outside only reshape to () and astype.
One streaming read of lp at HBM rate; VPU work is 3 ops per vreg with independent chains (no per-row lane reductions).

Grid (2, rows/4096) over the bitcast view (pair, B*C*H, W): blocks (4096, W) bf16, 1 MB per input; both axes arbitrary.
fori over 32-row chunks, f32 math, (8,W) f32 carry; pair 0 accumulates (sigmoid(x)-y)^2 (sigmoid via tanh), pair 1 the stable BCE-with-logits term; scratch (2,8,W).
Last step: 2*sqrt(mse+smooth) + bce. Outside: only the bitcast reshape and the scalar reshape/cast.
Speed idea: no relayout copy (a 1024-lane view would not be a bitcast), no block-sized temporaries; one HBM read.

Each (128 rows, 128 samples) tile of x and t is transposed in-kernel (rows -> lanes), so the 5 moment sums
(St, Sd, Stt, Sdd, Std with d = x - t) are plain VPU sublane adds and the per-row loss math runs lane-dense (1,128),
instead of 5 cross-lane (XLU) reductions per (16,256) chunk and per-row math (2 divides + log) on lane-sparse (16,1) vregs, which would make the kernel compute-bound, not HBM-bound.
centred moments come from the one-pass sums (shift-invariant, d form avoids x~t cancellation); a single HBM pass.
blocks of ~4 MiB per input (32 grid steps, "arbitrary", resident (1,128) f32 accumulator, vmem limit 48 MiB).

Grid (rows/4096,) over the bitcast view (B*C*H, W); in/out blocks (4096, W) f32 = 2 MiB, parallel axis.
Per element in f32: c = min(x, 50); sp = log1p(exp(c)); out = x * erf(sp) with the 13-term rational erf (clipped at 4).
Outside the kernel only the leading-dim reshape and its inverse (bitcasts); a 1024-lane reshape would cost two relayout copies.
Speed idea: a single HBM pass at XLA's rate.

Grid (B, C/16) = (8, 8); block (1, 16, 256, 256) f32 = 4 MiB in and out, on the original 4-D array (no reshape at all).
weight and bias go to SMEM as (C,) f32; each channel plane is x * w[c] + b[c] with scalar operands, in a fori over the 16 channels.
x is not reshaped to (B, C, H*W): that would change the tiled minor dims, so XLA would add a relayout copy before and after the kernel.
Speed idea: one read and one write of 268 MB each, nothing else; f32 math on the VPU is far below the HBM time.

Grid (B*C/cb,) "parallel" over a (B*C, H, W) view of x (leading-dim merge, a bitcast); in/out blocks (cb, H, W) f32 = 4 MB (cb=16).
weight and bias (C,) live whole in SMEM; plane k of step i uses channel (i*cb + k) % C as a scalar broadcast.
No accumulator: one fused multiply-add per element in f32, written straight to the output block.
Outside: only the bitcast reshapes (and astype on the 128-element params).
Speed idea: a (B*C, H*W) flatten would force relayout copies of input and output; native layout leaves one read + one write.

View inputs as (N0*N1, H, W) (leading-dim merge = bitcast). Grid (G/Gb,), Gb=32 slabs: blocks (32,128,128) f32 = 2 MB each,
3 inputs double-buffered = 12 MB (limit 40 MB). f32 math; sums over the leading block axis go into two (H, W) f32 scratches.
Last step: full reduce, max(count,1), scale, write (1,1) f32; slice + astype outside.
Speed idea: one pass over 402 MB at HBM rate with no relayout copies.

The depthwise runs on the VPU, not as 128 tiny per-channel banded MXU dots per 16-row step,
in a "row slab" layout: grid (N, H_out/64), stateless; x main block (1,C,64,W) plus
16-row halo blocks above/below; per 16-channel tile the window is widened to f32 VMEM so a sublane-strided load
gives one input row for 16 channels (vertical taps = different loads, no sublane shifts). Lane taps: f32 roll +
edge select, then pack to bf16 and do the 16 MACs in packed bf16 (2x VPU throughput); dw rows stored bf16 (R,C,W).
Pointwise per row: pw(O,C) @ dw(C,W) on the MXU (f32 acc) + bias, strided stores -> (O,16,W) groups -> bf16 out.

The depthwise 4x4 runs on the MXU: on the VPU it would cost 16 mul + 15 add per pixel plus unaligned
sublane relayouts for the kh taps, making the kernel VALU-bound.
per channel, Xs = [X, roll(X,1), roll(X,2), roll(X,3)] (rows of block+halo, bf16, K padded to 256) and
d_c = T_c @ Xs with T_c a banded Toeplitz-in-h weight (hb x 256, built outside with pad/concat only), f32 acc.
grid (B, cdiv(Hout,48)), x block (C,48,W) + 8-row halo; pointwise = bf16 MXU dot per row via sublane-strided
scratch loads; channel/copy loops unrolled x4; the last row block runs a masked, row-trimmed path.

A pipelined BlockSpec copy, not HBM->HBM DMAs from an ungridded kernel. grid=(L//tl + 1,), blocks (tl, N, E) on the native layout (~2 MiB each,
tl = largest divisor of L with tl*N*E*itemsize <= 2 MiB; 32 rows here), so in+out double buffers are ~8 MiB VMEM.
steps 0..L/tl-1 copy x block i to out block i; the extra last step writes the bias row into out
block L/tl (a partial edge block: only row L is in bounds, the rest is discarded). Its input index is
clamped to the last full block, so no extra input DMA. No float math outside; only bias.reshape(1, E).

Grid (N,), one image (3, 512, 512) per step, zero-padded into a (3, 528, 512) f32 VMEM copy; bf16 MXU, f32 accumulation.
Per pooled row (fori_loop, 64): 9 taps (3 channels x 3 lane shifts) of a 24-row aligned window stacked to (256, 512); one banded
matmul gives 8 conv rows x 16 channels; ReLU; a one-hot matmul sums the 8 rows; a folded matrix does the 8-column pooling and the
Linear(16->4) per 16-column group; rows land in a (1024,128) scratch and are gathered per channel by stride-16 loads.
Outside: only weight layout (transpose/pad/concatenate/broadcast/reshape) and the final output reshape.

Each INPUT row does one (KH*O=512, KW*C=512)@(512, W=256) bf16 matmul (kh in M, kw in K). A per-output-row (O,KH*KW*C)@(KH*KW*C,384)
matmul would latch the activations (2048x384 per 128 streamed rows) and spend 384 lanes on 259 columns; this layout gives a 4x smaller latch, 4x more
streamed rows, N=256 exactly; its KH row blocks are scattered into an f32 row accumulator (KH-1 rows carried across steps).
the 3 tail columns (W..OW-1) of all rows in a step come from ONE packed (512,512)@(512,128) matmul (4 lanes per row);
full steps are straight-line (no per-row branches or per-row pl.when blocks); grid (N, cdiv(OH,16)), native NCHW blocks, only weight layout outside.

Grid (R/4096,) over x viewed as (R, 128) (leading-dim merge, a bitcast); block (4096, 128) bf16, weights resident (hidden widths zero-padded to 128).
Two bf16 MXU layers with f32 accumulation, bias+ReLU in f32; layer 3 is dot_general(w3row (8,128), h2 (4096,128)) contracting lanes, so the outputs land along lanes.
Output (R/128, 128) f32, 32 dense rows per step; outside: reshape to (..., 1) and astype(bf16) only.
Speed idea: avoid the per-row lane reduction and the 128x-padded column stores inside the kernel; kernel is bound by the 67 MB read.

Grid (N/128 // 256,) over the (N/128, 128) bitcast view of x; each step holds 256 x 128 elements, "parallel".
In-kernel: transpose the tile so elements sit in sublanes, layer 1 as an MXU outer product with K1 (128, 128*latent) bf16, f32 bias
+ relu, layer 2 against a block-diagonal W2s (128, 4*128) so 4 elements' 32 outputs land in separate lane tiles; f32 accumulation.
Each (128, 32) piece is stored straight into the final (N/32, 32, 32) output block, so no relayout outside the kernel.
Outside the kernel: only broadcast/pad/reshape/slice/concatenate/astype to place w1, b1, w2, b2 (no tile, no arithmetic).

Grid (rows//tr, b//bb): x is reshaped to (b, c*bins, w) and read in blocks of (bb=2, tr=256, w). The batch axis is the last grid axis and is the reduction.
The kernel holds a float32 VMEM accumulator of shape (tr, w) and casts to bf16 when it stores on the last batch step.
The per-row centers column (tr, 1) is built outside the kernel with broadcast_to plus reshape only, instead of jnp.tile. All sigmoid and sum work runs inside the kernel.
The kernel is memory-bound: it streams 64 MB of bf16 input once and writes a small output. The row axis is parallel so it can be split across cores.

Reshaping (B,C,H,W)->(B,C,H*W) would change the TPU tiled HBM layout, so XLA would add two 128 MiB relayout copies,
and 512-lane chunks (64 vregs per operand) would spill. Instead x/target are viewed as (B, C, HW//128, 128) (a free bitcast when W==128),
blocks (1, C, 64, 128) f32 (4 MiB, vmem limit raised to 40 MiB), grid (B, R//64) = 32 steps, both "arbitrary" (one TC on v6e).
C is a leading untiled dim, so the softmax reduction is plain elementwise max/add across vregs (no sublane reductions): per 8-row
group, pass 1 = running max over 8-channel chunks, pass 2 = sum exp, sum t*(log t - x), sum t; result a + (m + log s) * st.
An (8,128) f32 scratch accumulates over the grid; the last step reduces it to a scalar and scales by 1/N. Outside: reshape/pad only.

Grid (B, H/32), blocks (1, C, 32, W) bf16 = 2 MiB for each of 2 inputs and 2 outputs, double-buffered (16 MiB) + 2 MiB f32 scratch.
Per 16-row chunk: pass 1 over channel groups of 8 computes e = exp(m + v/2) in f32, stores it in scratch and sums over channels;
pass 2 writes e/s and e^2 (exp(v)-1)/s^2. f32 throughout, bf16 on store.
Nothing outside the kernel: inputs and outputs keep their native NCHW layout (an H*W reshape would cost 4 relayout copies).
Speed idea: channel reduction is over a leading dim (vreg adds), one HBM pass of 256 MiB.

Kernel 1: grid over 64-row seq blocks of the z2 half ((64, B, Dh) bf16 via lane-block index 1); f32 LayerNorm;
writes zn (S, B, Dh) bf16 in the native layout.
Kernel 2: grid (Dh/128 lane chunks, S/512 row blocks); zn's (S, B, 128) chunk stays resident; at i == 0 it is
de-interleaved per batch row with 128-lane strided loads into (B, S, 128) bf16 scratch. Each step does B matmuls
W(512, S) @ zb[b] (bf16, f32 accumulate), adds bias, re-interleaves with strided stores into a (512*B, 128) f32
scratch, multiplies by the z1 block and stores bf16. Outside: only reshapes and the W slice/astype (layout ops).

Grid (B, H/th) parallel; data/gate/out blocks (1, C, th, W) in native NCHW layout, th multiple of 8 with C*th*W*4 ~ 2 MB (th=32).
Per group g: f32 carry (th, W) = sum_c gate_in[c] * w[c, g] (weights and bias as SMEM scalars), gate = max(tanh(acc + b), 0).
Then out[c] = data[c] * gate for the channels of group g. Outside only tiny reshapes of weight/bias to flat SMEM vectors.
Speed idea: no relayout copies, single HBM pass over both inputs, VPU-only contraction (C FMAs per pixel) instead of a skinny MXU matmul.

No stride-2 sublane load and no f32 scratch: Mosaic strided loads need a base memref whose last dim is exactly 128.
Pair rows through TPU bf16 packing instead: pltpu.bitcast of a (2r, C) bf16 chunk to int32 gives (r, C) words, each holding rows 2i and 2i+1 of one column.
Unpack in registers: (w << 16) and (w & 0xFFFF0000) bitcast to f32 are the two bf16 values exactly; out = a*a + b*b (= 2 * mean of the pair) in f32, cast on store.
Grid (batch, row-blocks), x block (1, TL<=2048, C), out block (1, TL/2, C), C lane-dense, both axes parallel; an inner fori_loop over 256-row chunks keeps temporaries small.
Speed: one HBM read of x and one write of the half-length output, no relayout copies, only VPU bit ops + 2 muls per output; nothing but an astype runs outside the kernel.

Outside: x NCHW -> NHWC transpose, W -> (kh*ci, kw*co) layout, final slice [:Wo] + NHWC -> NCHW transpose (layout ops only).
Grid (N,), "arbitrary": block (1,H,W,C) bf16 in, (1,Ho,W,Co) bf16 out, weights resident; standardized once (step 0) in f32 into a bf16 VMEM scratch.
Loop over groups of 5 output rows: lanes-concat the 4 input rows (K=512), one (640x512)@(512x512) bf16 MXU call, f32 accumulate.
kw folded by summing 4 column blocks after sublane rolls by kw (wrap only hits w >= Wo, sliced off); bias added in f32, cast on store.
Speed idea: big-M/K/N MXU calls with positions streamed, no in-kernel relayout passes.

Grid (B*C/4,), block (4, H, W) of the (B*C, H, W) view (leading-dim merge); fori_loop over the 4 planes.
Each plane: static loop over 32-row chunks; vertical diff via sublane roll, horizontal via lane roll, |.| summed unmasked into
(32, W) f32 carries; chunk-boundary vertical pairs from 1-row loads into a (1, W) carry.
Accumulators persist in VMEM scratch across the grid; on the last step mask row 0 / column W-1, reduce, scale, write (1,1).
Speed: no per-8-row serial loop; ~8 vector ops per input vreg, so the kernel is bound by the single 268 MB HBM read.

The transpose of topic_emb outside is (3,2,0,1) fused with astype(bf16) -> Y[a,b,j,k] (half the bytes of an f32 transpose written by XLA and re-read by the kernel).
tsw^T for 4 pairs at once is ONE stationary-weight matmul (4*J, K) @ w^T(K, Hd) instead of a per-pair w@X matmul.
pairs are processed two at a time: [E_p | E_q] (M, 2Hd) x blockdiag(tsw_p^T, tsw_q^T)^T gives S for both pairs as one lane-dense (M, 2J)=(128,128) tile,
so the softmax over M runs on full vregs and S costs one MXU pass per 2 pairs; H_p/H_q = P2 @ [T_p;0] / [0;T_q] (aligned zero-concats, no lane shifts).
grid (A, Bt/nb), nb=32 pairs per step; E/Y/T/out blocks on native layouts, bf16 MXU inputs with f32 accumulation and f32 softmax.

Grid (B, C/cb) over the original 4D shape, block (1, cb, H, W) with cb the largest channel count whose block is <= 4 MiB (4 x 512 x 512 f32 here).
No accumulator: the reference returns x itself (the TV loss is discarded), so the kernel is a copy.
Nothing outside the kernel; no reshape, so no relayout copy.
Speed idea: stage through VMEM with auto double-buffering instead of an HBM->HBM DMA.

x enters the kernel in native NCHW blocks; an XLA space-to-depth transpose of all 64 MB of x outside the kernel
would be a full relayout copy.
There, one exact bf16 0/1 matmul per 256 rows de-interleaves W by the stride (kw shifts = lane rolls, zero-padded).
conv1 = W1^T(64,512) @ window(512, 2x128 lanes) per row pair. One 128x128 transpose gives R' (H-shifted 2x2 phases).
conv2 is a 512-deep (2x2-tap) matmul on [R' | neighbour-mixed R'], built once per row. conv3 runs on column pairs
(N=128 fully used, K=768), so the 2x2 max-pool becomes a lane roll plus a leading-dim max. The fc layer runs in its own kernel.

Grid (B, HW/512) = (16, 8), "arbitrary"; z viewed as (B, C, HW) with block (1, 256, 512); codebook (1024, 256) and its transpose resident.
Step 0 splits the codebook into bf16 hi/mid/lo and ee = |e|^2 into VMEM scratch; each step splits z the same way and forms z.e with 6 bf16 MXU passes (f32 accumulation) so near-ties resolve like the reference's Precision.HIGHEST matmul.
d = (zz + ee) - 2*s in the reference's order, first-index argmin over codes, one-hot (bf16) times bf16 codebook^T gathers z_q; commitment loss accumulates in a resident (1,1) f32 output.
Outside: reshapes, the codebook transpose. Speed idea: one fused pass over z, MXU-bound at ~7 bf16 passes.

Grid (batch, H/8) per conv layer, block (1, 8, W, Cin) plus two 1-row halo blocks; weights resident as (3, Cin, 3*Cout).
Three bf16 MXU dots (one per kh) with f32 accumulation; the kw taps are combined with sublane rolls plus edge masks, then bias + ReLU in f32.
Fused 2x2 max-pool: H max in registers. For W, one f32 scratch of shape (n, 128) per 128-lane chunk of Cout, then a stride-2 sublane read. Mosaic only allows strided loads when the base memref's last dim is exactly 128.
First layer (Cin=3): im2col built with pad/slice/concat outside the kernel (layout ops only), then one matmul kernel.
Outside the kernels: only transpose, pad, reshape, concat and astype.

Grid (B*C*H/4096,) "arbitrary": blocks (4096, W) bf16 of the (B*C*H, W) bitcast view of each input (2 MB each).
Inside, 32-row chunks upcast to f32, e = y - y', f = e*tanh(e/2), folded into an (8, W) f32 value, added to an (8, W) scratch.
Last step reduces the scratch and multiplies by 1/n; only the final scalar reshape/astype is outside.
Speed idea: no (rows, 512) reshape, which would be a relayout copy doubling HBM traffic; one pass over 134 MB.

Grid (B,), one full (1, C, H, W) bf16 image per step (8 MB in + 8 MB out, double-buffered, 100 MB VMEM limit); no reshapes of x, so no relayout copies.
Pass 1 (in VMEM): per-channel sum and sum of squares in f32, 8 channels per fori_loop iteration so 8 reduction chains overlap; results lane-broadcast into (C,128) scratch.
Layer stats from the channel sums; one vectorized step builds per-channel scale a and shift b (rho blend of IN and LN, times this image's gamma, plus beta).
Pass 2: out = x*a + b, 8 channels per iteration, cast to bf16 on store.
Outside: only reshape/astype of gamma, beta (B,C)->(B,C,1) and rho (1,C,1,1)->(C,1).

Grid (B*C*H/4096,), block (4096, W) of the (B*C*H, W) view (leading-dim merge, a bitcast); 4 MB per block, double-buffered.
Inner fori_loop over 128-row slices (32 vregs): softplus(-x) = max(-x,0) + log(1 + exp(-|x|)) (2 EUP ops), summed to (8, W) f32.
(8, W) f32 accumulator in VMEM scratch across the grid; last step reduces to (1,1) and multiplies by 1/size.
Speed: few VALU ops per vreg and large inner steps, so the kernel is bound by the single 268 MB HBM read.

Grid (N, H/32): each step 2x2-average-pools a (C, 32, W) chunk (row pairs gathered from 128-lane slabs, column pairs and /4 by a
one-hot MXU matmul with a hi/lo bf16 split) into a padded bf16 (rows*C, W/2) scratch, rows ordered (h, c).
On the last row chunk: conv1 and conv2 as one (kw*Co, kh*Ci) @ (kh*C, W/2) bf16 matmul per output row (f32 acc), kw shifts by lane
roll + mask, bias, LeakyReLU; conv2 rows go to a 128-lane slab by strided store, then one store of the (Co, 128, 128) output block.
Outside: weight transpose/reshape/astype and the final slice to (126, 126). Speed: x read once, all intermediates in VMEM.

Grid (N, H/32) per conv layer, row tile 32 with p halo rows fetched as 1-row blocks; f32 VMEM scratch holds the zero-padded tile, inner fori_loop over ~1024-row chunks.
Conv = k bf16 MXU matmuls per chunk (kx taps concatenated along channels when C%128==0), f32 accumulation, bias+ReLU fused; 1x1 heads fused as post layers, conv1_1 fused as a pre 1x1 over a 3x3 im2col.
2x2 max pool fused into the producing conv: the row max is taken in registers, and the column max uses strided loads from a scratch shaped (ceil(co/128), ty/2, W, 128), so the strided load always sees a 128-wide last dim.
Outside the kernels: only transpose, pad, concatenate, reshape, astype, and slicing/reordering/zero-padding of the weights.

Grid (B, C/128) = (16, 4); block (1, 128, 128, 128) bf16 = 4 MiB on the native NCHW array (no reshape before the kernel).
Inner fori over groups of 8 channels: upcast to f32, sum over H (sublane axis) and over the W/128 lane chunks -> one (8, 128) vreg, stored into a (C, 128) f32 scratch.
Last channel block: transpose (C,128) -> (128,C), sum sublanes -> (1, C) style row, divide by H*W, L2-normalize, store (1, 1, C).
f32 accumulation; only the (B,1,C)->(B,C) reshape of 16 KB is outside.
Speed idea: one 268 MB read at HBM rate; x.reshape(b, c, h*w) would add a relayout copy of x.

Grid (N, C/64) ("parallel", "arbitrary"), input block (64, H, W) f32 = 4 MiB on the native 4D array, double-buffered 8 MiB; output block (C, 1) f32 resident across the channel axis.
No reshape of x: an (N, C, H*W) view would force a relayout copy of the whole 512 MiB input.
Per 8 channels: fold H into an (8, W) partial with vreg adds, then sublane and lane reduce to a (8, 1) column of means written into the output block.
Last channel step: L2-normalize the (C, 1) column in place (f32).
Outside the kernel: reshape (N, C, 1) -> (N, C) of the 32 KiB result.

Reshape x (free, layout-only) to (B*C, H/2, 2W) so each row holds input rows 2i and 2i+1 side by side in the lanes. Lane slices [0,W) and [W,2W) are aligned, so no strided sublane load is needed.
Grid is (B*C/8,), "parallel". Input blocks are (8, H/2, 2W) f32 (2 MiB each), output blocks (8, H/2, W/2). An in-kernel fori_loop handles one plane per iteration.
Rows: max of the even/odd row arrays plus sublane rolls with -inf masks. This gives 2-, 4- and 8-row window maxima at stride 2 directly.
Columns: lane rolls with -inf masks give the window maxima, and the three pools are summed. The even columns are then picked with an exact 0/1 selection matmul (f32 accumulate, HIGHEST precision) and scaled by 1/3.
Outside the kernel there are only reshapes. The kernel reads the input once from HBM and is bandwidth-bound.

Grid (N/8, C/64) with C last ("arbitrary"), blocks (8, 64, 8, 128) f32 = 2 MB of the native array, no outside reshape.
Scratch (8, 8, 128) f32 running max over channels (elementwise across vregs).
Last C step: for each of the 20 adaptive bins, masked lane max (keepdims) -> (bn,8,1); select limb row idx by a sublane mask,
weight by how often the limb appears, mean over the 5 parts, then the 20->20 adaptive mean, assembled into a (bn,1,20) block.
Output is written directly as (N,1,20). Speed: one HBM pass at streaming rate.

Grid over planes (b*c/8 steps, parallel); input block (8, h/2, 2w) after a free contiguous reshape so each row pair sits side by side; output block (8, h/2, w/2).
Row pool = max of the two lane halves (no strided loads). Column pool = roll+max, then a 0/1 selection matmul (f32, HIGHEST) picks the even columns.
The rest (edge-pad pool2 s1, pool3 p1) uses pltpu.roll plus iota masks that fall back to the center value at borders. Mean is computed in f32 in the kernel.
Outside the kernel there are only reshapes. The kernel reads the input once and writes the output once; double-buffered VMEM is about 5 MiB.
